content: In 1987, T.A.L. reported the emergence of tetracycline-resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae (TRNG) in the United States. Confirmed isolates of TRNG have been identified in 17 states. Additionally, unconfirmed reports based on disk-diffusion testing conducted in local laboratories have been noted in Alabama and the District of Columbia. Hedberg et al. (1990) described an outbreak of erythromycin-resistant staphylococcal conjunctivitis in a neonatal nursery, published in the Pediatric Infectious Disease Journal. Isenberg et al. (1995) conducted a controlled trial evaluating the use of povidone-iodine as prophylaxis against ophthalmia neonatorum, published in the New England Journal of Medicine. Ison et al. (1988) reported the presence of tetracycline-resistant gonococci in the United Kingdom, as documented in The Lancet. Knapp et al. (1987) detailed the frequency and distribution of N. gonorrhoeae strains with plasmid-mediated, high-level tetracycline resistance in the United States, published in the Journal of Infectious Diseases. Schwarcz et al. (1990) provided data on national surveillance of antimicrobial resistance in N. gonorrhoeae through the Gonococcal Isolate Surveillance Project, published in JAMA. Darling and McDonald (2010) performed a meta-analysis on the efficacy of ocular prophylactic agents for preventing gonococcal and chlamydial ophthalmia neonatorum, published in the Journal of Midwifery & Women’s Health. Kapoor et al. (2015) outlined interventions for preventing ophthalmia neonatorum in a protocol published in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews. Mabry-Hernandez and Koenig (2010) reaffirmed recommendations for preventive services in a publication by the Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality. Zuppa et al. (2011) discussed various prophylactic approaches for ophthalmia neonatorum in the Journal of Maternal-Fetal & Neonatal Medicine. Ali et al. (2007) compared the efficacy of betadine, erythromycin, and no prophylaxis for ophthalmia neonatorum in the Journal of Tropical Pediatrics. Brussieux et al. (1991) conducted a comparative study of silver nitrate and oxytetracycline eye drops for neonatal conjunctivitis prevention, published in Annales de Pédiatrie. Chen (1992) compared silver nitrate, tetracycline, erythromycin, and no prophylaxis for ophthalmia neonatorum. David et al. (2011) evaluated the use of 5% povidone-iodine and 1% tetracycline for preventing ophthalmia neonatorum, published in Ophthalmology. Fischer and Reta (1988) studied neonatal conjunctivitis prevention in Zaire, published in Annals of Tropical Pediatrics. Hammerschlag et al. (1989) assessed the efficacy of neonatal ocular prophylaxis for preventing chlamydial and gonococcal conjunctivitis, published in the New England Journal of Medicine. Hammerschlag et al. (1980) evaluated erythromycin ointment for neonatal chlamydial infection prophylaxis, published in JAMA. Hammerschlag et al. (1982) conducted longitudinal studies on chlamydial infections during the first year of life, published in the Pediatric Infectious Disease Journal. Isenberg et al. (2003) proposed a double-application approach for ophthalmia neonatorum prophylaxis, published in the British Journal of Ophthalmology. Isenberg et al. (1995) conducted a controlled trial of povidone-iodine for ophthalmia neonatorum prophylaxis, published in the New England Journal of Medicine. Laga et al. (1988) compared silver nitrate and tetracycline for preventing gonococcal and chlamydial ophthalmia neonatorum, published in the New England Journal of Medicine. Matinzadeh et al. (2007) evaluated the efficacy of topical ophthalmic prophylaxis for preventing ophthalmia neonatorum, published in Tropical Doctor. Ozkan et al. (1999) conducted a controlled trial on the efficacy and safety of povidone-iodine for ophthalmia neonatorum prophylaxis, published in Çocuk Sağlığı ve Hastalıkları Dergisi. Ramirez-Ortiz et al. (2007) compared 5% povidone-iodine eye drops and ophthalmic chloramphenicol for preventing neonatal conjunctivitis in a trachoma-endemic area in southern Mexico, published in the British Journal of Ophthalmology. Steigleder (1989) evaluated the efficacy of neonatal ocular prophylaxis for preventing chlamydial and gonococcal conjunctivitis, published in Zeitschrift für Hautkrankheiten. Zanoni et al. (1992) compared silver nitrate with erythromycin for ophthalmia neonatorum prophylaxis, published in Clinical Pediatrics. Deogan et al. (2010) conducted a cost-effectiveness analysis of a community-based intervention to reduce chlamydia prevalence in Sweden, published in the Scandinavian Journal of Public Health. Keenan et al. (2010) analyzed the cost of povidone-iodine for ophthalmia neonatorum prophylaxis, published in Archives of Ophthalmology. The International Drug Price Indicator Guide (2014 edition) provided additional cost-related references. Kakar et al. (2010) reported on Chlamydia trachomatis as a cause of neonatal conjunctivitis in a tertiary care center, published in the Indian Journal of Medical Microbiology.
